cultural.vision_reason: A carved wooden doll with a face, dressed in sealskin parka and trousers with a pointed hood—classic Inuit clothing and doll-making tradition, well documented as a genuine ethnographic type.

physical.title: doll
physical.summary: Doll, male, of wood, the head and torso carved in one piece, both legs carved separately, articulated with flange hinges on iron pins; the hands are carved separately without arms, the parka sleeves being shrunk to fit tight over the wrists. The head is carved with slight features, and burnt hair. Seal-skin clothing consists of a parka, with the pointed tip characteristic of the male hood, and trousers, both items sewn with sinew and probably originally haired.
